bg-07-01.why: 운동하다 always conjugates to 운동해요 in polite speech.

bg-07-01.q: State what you do at home using 집에서 and 요리해요.
bg-07-01.why: 요리하다 is an action verb taking the location marker 에서, and 하다 conjugates to 해요.

bg-07-01.hint: Verbs ending in -하다 always conjugate to -해요, never -하요.
bg-07-01.why: 하다 has an irregular contraction: 하다 becomes 해요, never 하요.

steps.en: I exercise in the park every day.
I exercise in the park every day.

en: Every morning, I exercise in the park.
And during the day, I study at the library.
In the evening, I cook delicious food at home.
On weekends, I clean my room cleanly.

bg-07-01.q: Where does the speaker exercise in the morning?
bg-07-01.why: The text states '저는 아침마다 공원에서 운동해요' (Every morning, I exercise in the park).

bg-07-01.q: What does the speaker do at home in the evening?
bg-07-01.why: The text says '저녁에는 집에서 맛있는 음식을 요리해요' (In the evening, I cook delicious food at home).

items: Turn activity nouns into verbs effortlessly by adding 하다
Conjugate any -하다 verb into the polite -해요 form

bg-07-02.why: 마셔요 said with an inviting intonation works as a friendly suggestion.

bg-07-02.q: Invite a friend to have lunch together using 같이 and 점심 먹어요.
bg-07-02.why: In Korean, plain polite form with an upbeat tone serves as an invitation ('Let's...').

bg-07-02.hint: The polite ending for the verb stem 먹- is 먹어요, not 먹이에요.
bg-07-02.why: 먹다 is an action verb with vowel ㅓ, taking -어요: 먹어요.

ko: 시간 있으면 우리 같이 커피 마셔요!
en: Where are you going right now?
I am going to the cafe.
If you have time, let's have coffee together!

bg-07-02.q: Where is the second speaker heading?
bg-07-02.why: The second speaker says '저는 카페에 가요' (I am going to the cafe).

bg-07-02.q: What does the first speaker suggest?
bg-07-02.why: The first speaker invites them saying '우리 같이 커피 마셔요!' (Let's have coffee together!).

items: Use polite endings for statements, questions, and suggestions without changing word order
Make friendly invitations with colleagues and friends using 우리 and 같이

bg-07-03.hint: Let's take a walk together in the park.
bg-07-03.why: 산책하다 becomes 산책해요, here serving as an enthusiastic invitation.

bg-07-03.q: Invite someone to take a walk in the park using 공원에서 and 산책해요.
bg-07-03.why: Pair the action location 공원에서 with the invitation 산책해요!.

bg-07-03.hint: Verbs ending in -하다 conjugate to -해요 in polite speech.
bg-07-03.why: 쇼핑하다 conjugates to 쇼핑해요, not 쇼핑하요.

base.en: I take a walk in the park.

steps.en: Let's walk in the park on the weekend.

en: The weather is really nice today.
Let's take a walk together in the park!
After walking, let's chat enjoyably at the cafe.
On the weekend, let's shop at the department store.

bg-07-03.q: Why does the speaker suggest a walk?
options: They are looking for a pet
bg-07-03.why: The passage starts with '오늘 날씨가 참 좋아요' (The weather is really nice today).

bg-07-03.q: Where will they chat after walking?
bg-07-03.why: The text says '카페에서 재미있게 이야기해요' (Let's chat enjoyably at the cafe).

items: Use various activity verbs (산책하다, 이야기하다, 쇼핑하다) in conversation
Suggest leisurely weekend activities with friends in Korean

bg-07-04.hint: I am studying at the library now.
bg-07-04.why: A statement answering what you are currently doing with a falling intonation.

bg-07-04.q: A friend asks “오늘 저녁에 뭐 해요?” Reply that you are resting at home using 집에서 and 쉬어요.
bg-07-04.why: Answer clearly as a statement with a falling intonation: 집에서 쉬어요.

bg-07-04.hint: 시작하다 conjugates to 시작해요 for suggestions and invitations.
bg-07-04.why: 시작하다 becomes 시작해요 in polite speech.

steps.en: I am studying at the library right now.
I am studying at the library right now.

ko: 민수 씨, 지금 어디에서 뭐 해요?
공부 끝나고 우리 같이 점심 먹어요!
좋아요, 열두 시에 학생 식당에서 만나요.
en: Minsu, where are you and what are you doing right now?
I am studying Korean at the library.
After studying, let's have lunch together!
Sounds good, let's meet at twelve at the student cafeteria.

bg-07-04.q: What is Minsu doing right now?
bg-07-04.why: Minsu answers '저는 도서관에서 한국어를 공부해요' (I am studying Korean at the library).

bg-07-04.q: Where and when will they meet for lunch?
bg-07-04.why: Minsu suggests '열두 시에 학생 식당에서 만나요' (Let's meet at twelve at the student cafeteria).

items: Distinguish between questions, statements, and invitations based on intonation and punctuation
Confidently participate in real-life Korean exchanges using -해요 and -어요
